info.title: Senders API
info.description:
Use the Senders API to create the sender identities used by Yext Email. A sender defines the address recipients see and, optionally, the address they use to reply. You can associate a sender with a Knowledge Graph Entity or create an account-level sender.

## Before You Begin

Configure your sending domain before creating a sender. If the response has a `verificationStatus` of `SENDER_IDENTITY_STATUS_PENDING`, complete the verification email flow before sending. Sender verification and domain verification are separate requirements; both must satisfy your account's sending policy.

## Authentication and Versioning

Send requests to `https://api.yextapis.com` with your app's API key in the `api-key` header or `api_key` query parameter. Include one fixed `v` date, such as `20240401`, and set `Content-Type: application/json`. Use your account ID or `me` in the URL.

## Entity and Account Senders

Set `email.entityId` to the exact Entity ID from Knowledge Graph to create an Entity sender. Omit it for an account-level sender. Sending an empty string is invalid.

## Response Format

Successful responses contain `meta` and `response`. The sender's `name` contains its Yext-assigned UUID. Check `response.verificationStatus` to determine whether verification is still required. Timestamps use RFC 3339 strings. Omit optional request fields you are not setting rather than sending `null`.

See [Policies and Conventions](https://docs.yext.com/docs/managementapis/introduction/overview-policies-and-conventions/) and [Errors](https://docs.yext.com/docs/managementapis/introduction/errors/) for shared Management API guidance.

post.description:
Creates an email sender for an Entity or the account.

Provide `email.emailAddress`. To associate the sender with a Knowledge Graph Entity, set `email.entityId` to its exact Entity ID. Omit that field for an account-level sender. You can also provide a reply-to address and display name.

The default `verificationMode` is `SENDER_VERIFICATION_MODE_REQUIRED`. Complete the verification email flow when the response status is pending. `SENDER_VERIFICATION_MODE_SKIP` requires an active, provider-verified domain and is unavailable for sandbox accounts. Both modes validate the sender's ownership and uniqueness.

A verified sender must still meet domain and sending requirements when used by a campaign. This method creates a sender; it does not update an existing sender or provide a request ID for duplicate detection.

default.description: An error occurred. See `meta.errors` for the error code and message.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: API version date in YYYYMMDD format. Use one fixed date for your integration; supply this parameter once per request.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: External account ID, or `me` for the credential's own account.

emailAddress.description: Valid email address used for replies. Header control characters are not allowed.

displayName.description: Display name shown with the reply-to address. Maximum 40 Unicode characters. Header control characters are not allowed.

emailAddress.description: Sender email address shown to recipients. Normalized and validated before creation. The domain must meet your account's sending requirements.

entityId.description: Entity ID from Knowledge Graph. Omit for an account-level sender; an empty string is invalid. Each Entity can have one sender identity. Different Entities can use the same email address.

replyTo.description: Address and display name used for replies. Does not change the sender address or its Entity association.

mailPublicEmailSender.description: Public sender contracts use Knowledge Graph external entity IDs. The existing Sender contracts retain numeric IDs for generated internal clients.
mailPublicEmailSender.title: mailPublicEmailSender

channel.description: Email is the supported channel: SENDER_CHANNEL_EMAIL.

email.description: Email address, optional Entity association, and reply-to settings.

verificationStatus.description: PENDING means the sender must complete the verification email flow. VERIFIED means sender identity verification is complete. Domain and sending requirements still apply.

verifiedAt.description: Time sender verification completed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Absent or null when the sender is not verified.

name.description: Complete resource name: accounts/{account}/senders/{sender}. Both the account segment and sender UUID are assigned by Yext.
